# UI Atlas: sources

84 libraries, tools and references. Check the licence before shipping anything copied from them. "Inspiration only" means look, do not copy.

- **[98.css](https://jdan.github.io/98.css/)** `98-css`: Windows title bars, Tree view, Tabs. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* see site. *Note:* CSS only: draggable windows and desktop behavior require separate JS.
- **[Aceternity UI](https://ui.aceternity.com/explore)** `aceternity`: Interactive marketing components and hover-driven cards. *Licence:* Free components and paid Pro; verify the selected component license. Site terms reserve redistribution rights.. *Install:* npx shadcn@latest add @aceternity/3d-card. *Note:* This directory links upstream examples and uses original studies; it does not redistribute Aceternity source.
- **[Adobe Leonardo](https://leonardocolor.io)** `adobe-leonardo`: Contrast-first, accessible colour scales and themes. *Licence:* Apache-2.0. *Install:* npm install @adobe/leonardo-contrast-colors. *Note:* Targets WCAG 2 contrast; check APCA separately if you use it.
- **[Amicro](https://amicro.dev/)** `amicro`: Tactile card spreads, morphing controls and spring-based micro-interactions. *Licence:* MIT (2026 SYED SUBHAN UDDIN); retained in AMICRO_LICENSE.txt.. *Install:* Copy the selected MIT component from the repository. *Note:* Actual CardScatterSpread pinned to dc2a183, with original artwork and a keyboard/touch toggle.
- **[Animate UI](https://animate-ui.com/)** `animate-ui`: Polished motion on familiar product UI patterns. *Licence:* MIT + Commons Clause; application use allowed, original components cannot be sold or redistributed as a kit. *Install:* npx shadcn@latest add @animate-ui/components-radix-tabs. *Note:* The local tabs demo uses actual source with original content. Retain the license; choose the matching primitive family for your application.
- **[Anime.js](https://animejs.com/documentation/)** `anime-js`: Staggered timelines, SVG morphing, Text animation. *Licence:* MIT public engine. *Install:* see site. *Note:* Animation engine requires composing your own components and cleaning up animations in framework lifecycles.
- **[Atlas colour themes](https://tng4480.github.io/design-demo/colour-themes.html)** `atlas-colours`: Compare complete dark palettes, accent pairings and semantic colour roles. *Licence:* Original study; Graphite colours supplied by the user. *Install:* Use colour-themes.json or export the selected CSS tokens. *Note:* Contrast checks cover selected pairs. Disabled text is for inactive controls only.
- **[Atlassian Design System](https://atlassian.design/)** `atlassian-business`: Project collaboration and contextual navigation. *Licence:* See individual package terms; local study is original. *Install:* See Atlassian Design System. *Note:* The study is an independent board, not an Atlassian implementation.
- **[Awesome Design Skills](https://github.com/bergside/awesome-design-skills)** `awesome-design-skills`: Choose a single style recipe before implementing a page. *Licence:* See the upstream repository; local example markup and styles are original. *Install:* see site. *Note:* The local demo selects the Editorial recipe. It does not represent all recipes or promise automatic quality improvements.
- **[Barba.js](https://barba.js.org/)** `barba`: Editorial page-to-page transitions. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* npm install @barba/core. *Note:* Requires lifecycle cleanup, focus restoration, page titles, navigation history and analytics handling. Avoid adding a second router to a React framework app.
- **[Bklit UI](https://bklit.com)** `bklit`: Expressive dashboards and animated data storytelling. *Licence:* Chart source MIT; Studio proprietary and cannot be reused/resold/redistributed without permission. *Install:* npx shadcn@latest add @bklit/line-chart. *Note:* Chart library and hosted Studio have different licenses
- **[Bruno Simon](https://bruno-simon.com/)** `bruno-simon`: Interactive 3D worlds and playful portfolio navigation. *Licence:* Portfolio inspiration; verify repository/asset terms independently. *Install:* No component install. *Note:* A bespoke experience rather than reusable application UI
- **[Cloudscape Design System](https://cloudscape.design/)** `cloudscape-business`: Resource lists and contextual detail panels. *Licence:* Apache 2.0; local study is original. *Install:* See Cloudscape documentation. *Note:* Local work is an independent study, not a Cloudscape component.
- **[Codrops](https://tympanus.net/codrops/)** `codrops`: Experimental interactions with accompanying tutorials and demo repos. *Licence:* Per-demo repository; no blanket license assumed. *Install:* Follow each tutorial repository. *Note:* Check the exact demo license, asset rights and dependencies
- **[ColorKit.io](https://colorkit.io/)** `colorkit`: Constructing stepped color scales for tokens and charts. *Licence:* Hosted tool; code license and pricing not established. *Install:* Enter start/end colors and blend-step count. *Note:* This exact domain is a color blender; do not conflate it with colorkit.tools or colorkit.app
- **[colors.co — unresolved](https://colors.co)** `colors-requested`: Preserved user-supplied source. *Licence:* Unknown. *Install:* None verified. *Note:* Exact domain could not be fetched. Coolors at coolors.co is a likely intended alternative but was not silently substituted
- **[Componentry](https://componentry.dev)** `componentry`: Distinctive hero effects, experimental type, editorial portfolios. *Licence:* MIT; dependencies have separate terms. *Install:* npx shadcn@latest add @componentry/cursor-driven-particle-typography. *Note:* Validate touch, reduced motion and performance per component; dense particles can be expensive The three selected demos run actual upstream React source at b602c28 with original control panels; Scroll Choreography uses its documented public Unsplash images.
- **[Coolors](https://coolors.co)** `coolors`: Fast palette generation and exploring color combinations. *Licence:* Hosted service; free and paid features. *Install:* Use browser generator. *Note:* Added separately from the unresolved colors.co. Main domain blocked crawler; linked official help verifies palette export.
- **[coss ui](https://coss.com/ui)** `coss-ui`: Refined product controls, composed input and chat composer patterns. *Licence:* Open-source component library; verify the exact component license and dependency terms before reuse. *Install:* Follow the component installation instructions. *Note:* Origin UI now redirects to coss ui. Source reference only in this gallery; its components are not reproduced locally.
- **[CSS scroll-driven animations](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_scroll-driven_animations)** `css-scroll-driven`: Reading progress, reveals and parallax without scroll listeners. *Licence:* Web platform feature; no licence needed. *Install:* No install: animation-timeline: scroll() / view(). *Note:* Chromium and Safari 26; check Firefox before relying on it. Always wrap in @supports.
- **[css-doodle](https://css-doodle.com/)** `css-doodle`: Generative grids, Polygon shapes, Random decorative patterns. *Licence:* MIT component; public doodles MIT per current service terms. *Install:* see site. *Note:* Large DOM grids can be expensive. Good for decorative surfaces, not functional widget primitives.
- **[D3](https://d3js.org)** `d3`: Bespoke charts, maps and diagrams with full control. *Licence:* ISC. *Install:* npm install d3. *Note:* Low level; use Plot first for standard charts.
- **[daisyUI](https://daisyui.com/components/)** `daisyui`: Diff comparison, Mockup window, Themeable cards. *Licence:* MIT public library; paid products separate. *Install:* see site. *Note:* CSS classes provide styling; complex widget behavior still needs application code.
- **[Design Prompts](https://www.designprompts.dev/)** `design-prompts`: Choose whole-page typography, colour and composition before selecting UI components. *Licence:* Publicly accessible prompt gallery; a reuse license for site source code, photos and assets was not verified. *Install:* Browse a style, inspect its full-page preview, then open Get Prompt. *Note:* Four original local compositions demonstrate Newsprint, Swiss Minimalist, Botanical and Maximalism. Full-page references remain linked. These are art-direction studies, not an upstream component library or copied prompts. Botanical uses original SVG illustrations. Some source light/dark labels differ from the observed preview appearance.
- **[Drei / React Three Fiber](https://drei.docs.pmnd.rs/)** `drei-react-three-fiber`: MeshTransmissionMaterial, Float, Stars, AsciiRenderer. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* see site. *Note:* 3D foundation rather than drop-in DOM UI. Requires GPU, camera/light setup, asset work and fallback.
- **[Fancy Components](https://fancycomponents.dev)** `fancy-components`: Playful text effects and micro-interactions. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* Copy from fancycomponents.dev. *Note:* React only; copy components individually.
- **[fffuel](https://fffuel.co)** `fffuel`: Grain, gradients, blobs, patterns and textures as SVG. *Licence:* Free tools; check the site's terms for each asset. *Install:* Use in the browser and export SVG. *Note:* Hosted tools, no code library.
- **[Framer Marketplace](https://www.framer.com/marketplace/components/)** `framer`: Rapid site composition with designer-editable assets. *Licence:* Per-asset; free and paid; selected shaders Single-Use. *Install:* Copy asset URL into Framer canvas. *Note:* A Framer asset is not automatically reusable React source outside Framer
- **[Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/)** `google-fonts-business`: Comparing readable typefaces and pairings. *Licence:* Font licenses vary by family; inspect the chosen family. *Install:* Use the chosen font family CSS. *Note:* Font loading depends on Google Fonts; fallbacks are provided.
- **[GSAP + ScrollTrigger](https://gsap.com/)** `gsap`: Precisely sequenced marketing stories and editorial motion. *Licence:* Custom Standard License; free commercial use including formerly premium plugins. Restrictions apply to competing visual animation builders; AI-generated GSAP code is explicitly allowed.. *Install:* npm install gsap. *Note:* Animation timelines, pinning, scrubbing, SVG morphs and text reveals
- **[Haikei](https://haikei.app/)** `haikei`: Layered waves, Blobs, Stacked peaks. *Licence:* Asset export rights not independently verified. *Install:* see site. *Note:* Exported static assets, not animated interactive components.
- **[Humanizer](https://github.com/blader/humanizer)** `humanizer`: Editing generic or inflated writing while preserving meaning. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* Read .agents/skills/humanizer/SKILL.md in the design-demo repository. *Note:* The preview is a fixed example, not an AI-powered editor. The project-local skill guides agents working in this repository.
- **[IBM Carbon Design System](https://carbondesignsystem.com/)** `carbon-business`: Enterprise data tables, filtering and information-rich dashboards. *Licence:* Apache 2.0; local study is original. *Install:* See Carbon component documentation. *Note:* Local work is inspired by the documented patterns and does not use Carbon components.
- **[Impeccable](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable)** `impeccable`: Refine an existing UI while preserving the chosen visual identity. *Licence:* See the upstream repository; local example markup and styles are original. *Install:* see site. *Note:* The local lab demonstrates selected guidance; it is not a complete skill workflow or measured benchmark. Upstream includes CLI tools and optional hooks.
- **[Khroma](https://www.khroma.co/)** `khroma`: Personalized palette, typography and gradient comparisons. *Licence:* Hosted tool; code license not established. *Install:* Choose preferred colors to train the browser-based generator. *Note:* Color proposals still need contextual accessibility testing
- **[Kibo UI](https://www.kibo-ui.com/)** `kibo-ui`: Richer product interactions: comparison, kanban, Gantt, editors and colour picking. *Licence:* MIT for the public component source. *Install:* npx shadcn@latest add @kibo-ui/comparison. *Note:* Large components have additional dependencies. The local comparison demo uses actual Kibo source with a small keyboard adapter and original SVG artwork.
- **[Kokonut UI](https://kokonutui.com)** `kokonut`: Polished controls, AI inputs, compact product cards. *Licence:* Free catalog MIT; Pro templates separately paid. *Install:* npx shadcn@latest add @kokonutui/particle-button. *Note:* Premium template access differs from free component license
- **[Land-book](https://land-book.com)** `land-book`: Curated landing pages by industry and style. *Licence:* Inspiration only. *Install:* Browse. *Note:* Look, do not copy.
- **[Lando Norris](https://landonorris.com/)** `lando-norris`: A distinctive interactive 3D product or personality hero. *Licence:* Inspiration only; source models, photography, branding and code are not licensed for reuse. *Install:* No component package; this is a bespoke website reference. *Note:* Requires model/material production, hit testing or a reveal mask, pointer/touch handling, reduced motion and performance fallbacks. The local study uses original procedural geometry and a screen-space reveal shader.
- **[Lenis](https://lenis.dev/)** `lenis`: Optional smooth scrolling and synchronized parallax. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* npm install lenis. *Note:* Smooths native scrolling; synchronizes scroll position with GSAP or WebGL. Does not create animation timelines itself.
- **[liquid-glass (nikdelvin)](https://github.com/nikdelvin/liquid-glass)** `liquid-glass-svg`: Apple Liquid Glass-style refraction with no WebGL. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* Copy the SVG filter and CSS. *Note:* backdrop-filter:url() refracts in Chromium; Safari falls back to blur. For WebGL refraction see liquidGL.
- **[Lucide](https://lucide.dev)** `lucide`: The default stroke icon set for product UI. *Licence:* ISC. *Install:* npm install lucide. *Note:* One stroke style; use Phosphor when you need weights.
- **[Lusion](https://lusion.co/)** `lusion`: 3D storytelling and high-end visual direction. *Licence:* Inspiration only; site assets not licensed for reuse. *Install:* No component install. *Note:* Large custom-production effort; study the ideas rather than treating as a component kit
- **[M3E (Material 3 Expressive web components)](https://matraic.github.io/m3e)** `m3e`: Material 3 Expressive shapes, motion and components on the web. *Licence:* MIT; community project, not affiliated with Google. *Install:* npm install @m3e/web. *Note:* Google has no official Expressive web library; Material trademarks belong to Google.
- **[Magic UI](https://magicui.design/docs/components/magic-card)** `magic-ui`: Magic Card, Animated Beam, Retro Grid, Comic Text. *Licence:* MIT for public repo; Pro separate. *Install:* npx shadcn@latest add @magicui/comic-text. *Note:* Strong marketing effects; combine selectively with quieter product controls.
- **[Manus](https://manus.im)** `manus`: Rapid whole-site prototyping and app exploration. *Licence:* Commercial service; generated application ownership advertised; inspect export dependencies separately. *Install:* Use Manus web app. *Note:* A building tool rather than a component library; public pricing page did not expose plan amounts to crawler
- **[Mobbin](https://mobbin.com)** `mobbin`: Real app flows: onboarding, settings, checkout, paywalls. *Licence:* Commercial service. *Install:* Browse. *Note:* Paid tiers; screenshots belong to the apps shown.
- **[Motion](https://motion.dev)** `motion`: Shared layout transitions, gestures, state-driven UI animation. *Licence:* Core MIT; Motion+ examples and UI separately paid. *Install:* npm install motion. *Note:* Public live previews do not imply premium source is free
- **[Motion-Primitives](https://motion-primitives.com)** `motion-primitives`: Composable text and interface transitions with controlled entry and exit. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* npx shadcn@latest add https://motion-primitives.com/r/text-effect.json. *Note:* Connect the trigger to the active section. These are section-triggered transitions, not continuously scrubbed animation.
- **[Neobrutalism Components](https://www.neobrutalism.dev/docs)** `neobrutalism-components`: Hard-shadow buttons, Bold bordered cards, Forms with flat color surfaces. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* see site. *Note:* Opinionated thick borders and shadows can overwhelm dense dashboards.
- **[NES.css](https://nostalgic-css.github.io/NES.css/)** `nes-css`: Pixel buttons, Speech balloons, Pixel containers. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* see site. *Note:* Provides components rather than page layout. Retro typography can reduce density/readability.
- **[Observable Plot](https://observablehq.com/plot)** `observable-plot`: Clear explanatory and exploratory charts in very little code. *Licence:* ISC. *Install:* npm install @observablehq/plot. *Note:* Styling defaults are plain; apply your tokens and direct labels.
- **[Open Props](https://open-props.style/)** `open-props`: Gradient tokens, Shadow scales, Easing and animation tokens. *Licence:* License file exists; exact terms not verified in this pass. *Install:* see site. *Note:* Token foundation rather than a component collection.
- **[Osmo](https://www.osmo.supply/)** `osmo`: Fast premium creative-site interactions. *Licence:* Commercial membership license; project implementation allowed. No redistribution as a component library or stockpiling resources outside Vault for future use. Legitimate existing project implementations may continue after cancellation.. *Install:* Use the official platform. *Note:* Link premium resources; directory demos should use original implementations.
- **[Paper Shaders](https://shaders.paper.design/)** `paper-shaders`: Neuro Noise, Liquid Metal, Fluted Glass, Halftone Dots, Mesh Gradient. *Licence:* Apache-2.0. *Install:* npm install @paper-design/shaders@0.0.81. *Note:* README explicitly asks to pin dependency: breaking changes can occur under 0.0.x versions. Keep LICENSE/NOTICE when redistributing library code. Neuro Noise runs the actual 0.0.81 vanilla shader locally, with official preset values observed in the Paper customizer. WebGL2 is required; offscreen instances are disposed and global pause stops animation.
- **[Phosphor Icons](https://phosphoricons.com)** `phosphor`: Icons in six weights (thin to duotone) for expressive interfaces. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* npm install @phosphor-icons/web. *Note:* Pick one weight per interface.
- **[React Bits](https://reactbits.dev/get-started/index)** `react-bits`: Aurora, Silk, Orb, Blur Text, Rotating Text, Tilted Card, Glass Icons, Pixel Transition. *Licence:* MIT + Commons Clause. *Install:* npx shadcn@latest add @react-bits/Aurora-JS-CSS. *Note:* MIT + Commons Clause permits use within applications, websites and products; it prohibits redistributing the components themselves. This gallery bundles eight actual components into demo applications, retains the license and links to the pinned upstream source. WebGL2 backgrounds need a fallback; the Tilted Card interaction is pointer-based.
- **[Realtime Colors](https://www.realtimecolors.com/)** `realtime-colors`: See palette roles on real site layouts and export tokens. *Licence:* Free hosted tool; export terms should be checked for your use. *Install:* Use browser toolbar. *Note:* Check contrast for every foreground/background pairing
- **[Recent (formerly Godly)](https://recent.design)** `recent-design`: Current, ambitious web design examples. *Licence:* Inspiration only. *Install:* Browse. *Note:* godly.website redirects here. Look, do not copy.
- **[Refero](https://refero.design)** `refero`: Searchable web app screens and components. *Licence:* Commercial service. *Install:* Browse. *Note:* Paid tiers.
- **[ReUI](https://reui.io/)** `reui`: Dense business UI: data grids, filters, schedules, kanban and application shells. *Licence:* Free component catalog plus separately paid Pro blocks; verify the terms of the selected item. *Install:* Use the installation command on the selected free component page. *Note:* Free components and paid blocks have different scope. This is a linked source reference; no Pro block source is copied.
- **[reveal.js](https://revealjs.com)** `reveal-js`: Slide decks as web pages with notes, fragments and PDF export. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* npm install reveal.js. *Note:* Default themes look dated; bring your own type and tokens.
- **[Rive](https://rive.app)** `rive`: Interactive vector animation driven by state machines. *Licence:* Web runtime MIT; editor is a hosted product. *Install:* npm install @rive-app/canvas. *Note:* Needs .riv files made in the Rive editor, so no local study here. Name the state machine explicitly in code.
- **[Rough.js](https://roughjs.com/)** `rough-js`: Sketchy rectangles, Hachure fills, Hand-drawn SVG paths. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* see site. *Note:* Drawing engine rather than accessible controls. Use semantic HTML for interaction and SVG for decorative treatment.
- **[Satori](https://github.com/vercel/satori)** `satori`: Generating Open Graph images per page at build or request time. *Licence:* MPL-2.0. *Install:* npm install satori. *Note:* Supports a subset of CSS (flexbox only); fonts must be passed in.
- **[shadcn-svelte](https://shadcn-svelte.com/docs)** `shadcn-svelte`: Dialog, Command, Data table. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* see site. *Note:* Community-led port; use when Svelte is your implementation target.
- **[shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components)** `shadcn-ui`: Resizable workspace, Dashboard and sidebar blocks, Interactive charts, Registry directory, Current style families. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* see site. *Note:* Excellent functional baseline but visual distinction needs your own tokens. Accessibility still depends on composition.
- **[Shader Gradient](https://shadergradient.co)** `shadergradient`: Fluid 3D hero surfaces, gradient mesh and atmospheric backgrounds. *Licence:* MIT upstream. *Install:* npm install @shadergradient/react@2.4.20 @react-three/fiber@9.3.0 three@0.180.0. *Note:* GPU load and React/R3F compatibility matter; avoid mounting many simultaneous canvases The local scroll system now runs the actual 2.4.20 renderer. Its choreography is original, and it uses no Framer/Figma screen captures. The earlier Atmospheric Mesh remains a CSS study.
- **[Skiper UI](https://skiper-ui.com/)** `skiper-ui`: Compact micro-interactions, expanding galleries and spatial motion. *Licence:* Selected free components permit personal/commercial use and modification with attribution; Pro components have separate terms.. *Install:* npx shadcn@latest add @skiper-ui/skiper52. *Note:* Runs selected free Skiper41/52/106/99/19/31 components with attribution. The stairs preloader is an independent study of visible Skiper9 behaviour. Adaptations, contained scroll and keyboard/touch wrappers are documented.
- **[Souradip](https://souradip.com/)** `souradip`: Immersive portfolio storytelling with a distinctive crafted visual world. *Licence:* Inspiration only; original site footage, artwork and code are not licensed for redistribution. *Install:* see site. *Note:* Browser inspection found two video elements and no canvas. Scroll/click triggers cinematic chapter changes. Footage and illustration production, media loading, navigation and reduced motion are major implementation concerns. The local demo uses original real-time Three.js geometry, not the source’s videos or assets.
- **[Spline](https://spline.design/)** `spline`: Interactive 3D objects, material studies, physical interactions and product scenes. *Licence:* Hosted platform and scene-specific rights; an embed does not grant an asset reuse license.. *Install:* npm install @splinetool/runtime, then load your exported scene URL. *Note:* Reviewed the official library and Mini Home template. No local Spline scene is included: the runtime and scene loading were too heavy for this atlas. Retained as a tool reference; use your own exported scene and measure loading/GPU cost.
- **[Stencil Wiki: Riso ink colours](https://www.stencil.wiki/colors)** `riso-inks`: Screen approximations (hex) of real Riso inks for two- and three-colour designs. *Licence:* Reference. *Install:* Look up. *Note:* Hex values are approximate; ask your printer which inks they stock.
- **[Tabler Icons](https://tabler.io/icons)** `tabler-icons`: Consistent icons for navigation, actions, dashboards and product controls. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* npm install @tabler/icons@3.49.0. *Note:* Use accessible labels on icon-only buttons; decorative icons should be hidden from assistive technology. Ship the icons you use instead of bundling the complete collection in a product.
- **[Taste Skill](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill)** `taste-skill`: Explore distinctive public-facing pages and creative sites. *Licence:* See the upstream repository; local example markup and styles are original. *Install:* see site. *Note:* The local lab shows selected v2 guidance only. Upstream has strict style bans, direction-draw scripts, imagery and motion floors, and an inspector; the full workflow was not executed.
- **[tsParticles](https://particles.js.org/samples)** `tsparticles`: Polygon mask, Confetti, Fireworks, Animated stars. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* see site. *Note:* Load only required engine/plugins and reduce particle density on mobile.
- **[tweakcn](https://tweakcn.com/)** `tweakcn`: Compare real colour, radius, typography and shadow systems before implementation. *Licence:* Apache-2.0 for the public editor source; exported presets are demonstrated with retained attribution. *Install:* Export a theme from the official editor or install its provided registry URL. *Note:* Local demo samples six actual theme token sets; it is not the full editor. Custom fonts use system fallbacks until you supply them.
- **[Tyler Hobbs: Flow Fields](https://tylerxhobbs.com/words/flow-fields)** `flow-fields-essay`: Understanding and tuning flow-field generative art. *Licence:* Reading reference. *Install:* Read. *Note:* Technique reference; the artworks are the artist's.
- **[Uiverse](https://uiverse.io/)** `uiverse`: Buttons, Toggle switches, Loaders. *Licence:* Official site states all UI elements MIT. *Install:* see site. *Note:* Community quality varies. Check each snippet's semantics, keyboard behavior and CSS isolation.
- **[Unicorn Studio](https://unicorn.studio)** `unicorn-studio`: Designer-built shader heroes and effects without writing GLSL. *Licence:* Commercial; the free plan prohibits commercial use. *Install:* Embed SDK from the editor. *Note:* Scenes live in an account, so no local study here. Check plan terms before client work.
- **[Vanta.js](https://www.vantajs.com/)** `vanta-js`: Drop-in interactive animated hero backgrounds. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* npm install vanta@0.5.24 three@0.134.0 p5@1.1.9. *Note:* Official site recommends at most one or two instances on a page, warns of slow WebGL on older devices and mobile incompatibility, and requires a fallback. This gallery uses actual Vanta with its documented older Three.js version isolated from modern Three.js demos. TOPOLOGY uses pinned p5.js 1.1.9 rather than WebGL; its 4,500 particle strokes form an autonomous flow field. The p5.js LGPL license is included in library notices.
- **[Vaul](https://vaul.emilkowal.ski/)** `vaul`: Touch drawer, Snap points, Nested drawer. *Licence:* MIT. *Install:* see site. *Note:* Actual Vaul 1.1.2 runs in the local drawer study. Upstream currently marks the project unmaintained; validate touch, scrolling and focus in your actual app.
- **[View Transitions API](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/view-transitions)** `view-transitions-api`: List-to-detail morphs and page transitions without a library. *Licence:* Web platform feature; no licence needed. *Install:* No install: document.startViewTransition(). *Note:* Same-document transitions are Baseline since October 2025; cross-document transitions are Chromium and Safari 18.2+ only.
- **[Watermelon UI](https://ui.watermelon.sh)** `watermelon`: Practical SaaS interaction patterns and realistic dashboard compositions. *Licence:* Free MIT; no Pro tier claimed by official docs. *Install:* npx shadcn@latest add https://registry.watermelon.sh/r/expandable-event-card.json. *Note:* Copying source means maintaining it; animation-heavy SSR usage needs client boundaries
- **[Webflow Interactions with GSAP](https://webflow.com/feature/interactions-animations)** `webflow-interactions`: Visually maintained motion for non-code teams. *Licence:* Webflow platform terms; underlying GSAP custom license. *Install:* Use the official platform. *Note:* Breakpoint, reduced-motion and page-scope controls are supported. Native element-specific navbar/tab/dropdown/slider triggers have limitations; review current help docs.
